name: Sele

attributes.attribute: word of many senses across Britain and Scotland
a sun goddess and the echo of Sele under her court

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sele is a British and Scottish folkloric figure. The name also appears as Seelie. Variations occur across Britain and Scotland. The word stands for fairy folk, sacred hills, folkloric figures, and festivals. Sele is not clearly of Celtic origin. It ties to Old Norse saell, which means happy, and to old terms for blessed. The Old Germanic roots gave the word a wide and loose reach, so its referents stayed varied. The Seelie Court, a troop of good fairies, and the Unseelie Court, a host of harmful ones, both come from this root. Later lore joins Sele to the Mermaid, the Silkie, and the sun goddess Sul.
